subject: microbiology
title: Line Probe Assay, IGRA, Tuberculin Test, BCG, MDR-TB and Niacin Test

steps.tx: A **line probe assay** amplifies mycobacterial DNA and hybridises products to probes arranged as lines on a strip. Wild type and mutation bands reveal resistance associated changes in genes such as rpoB for rifampicin, katG and inhA for isoniazid, and selected fluoroquinolone and injectable targets on second line assays. Missing wild type bands can indicate resistance even when a specific mutation probe is absent.
steps.say: LPA converts resistance mutations into a band pattern much faster than growth based susceptibility testing.

left.title: First line LPA
points: rpoB predicts rifampicin resistance
katG usually high level isoniazid resistance
inhA promoter often low level isoniazid resistance
Works best on smear positive specimens and isolates

right.title: Second line LPA
points: gyrA and gyrB for fluoroquinolones
rrs and eis for injectable agents
Guides MDR and pre XDR regimen construction
Sequencing can resolve discordant results

steps.tx: An **interferon gamma release assay** measures T cell interferon gamma after stimulation with Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens such as ESAT 6 and CFP 10. These antigens are absent from BCG and most environmental mycobacteria, improving specificity in vaccinated people. Like tuberculin testing, IGRA identifies immune sensitisation consistent with infection but cannot by itself distinguish latent infection from active tuberculosis disease.
steps.say: IGRA detects tuberculosis immune memory, not the anatomical presence of active disease.

left.title: Benefits
points: Single blood collection visit
Not boosted by prior BCG vaccination
No reader measurement of skin induration
Objective laboratory cutoff

right.title: Limits
points: Cannot separate latent from active disease
Indeterminate results occur with immune suppression
Conversion and reversion occur near cutoff
Laboratory processing time affects validity

steps.tx: The **tuberculin skin test** injects purified protein derivative intradermally and measures transverse induration, not erythema, after 48 to 72 hours. Cutoffs vary with risk and immune state because positive predictive value changes with prevalence and consequences. False negatives arise with HIV, recent infection, overwhelming tuberculosis, malnutrition and technical errors; false positives can reflect BCG or nontuberculous mycobacteria, especially with smaller reactions.
steps.say: Measure raised induration at two to three days and interpret it using the patient's risk category.

left.title: Technique
points: Intradermal injection raises a wheal
Read within 48 to 72 hours
Record millimetres of induration
Do not record erythema as the result

right.title: Interpretation
points: Five millimetres can be positive in high risk immunosuppression
Ten millimetres is used in many intermediate risk groups
Fifteen millimetres suits low risk populations in some guidelines
Active disease requires microbiological investigation

steps.tx: **BCG vaccine** is live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis given to reduce severe childhood tuberculosis, especially miliary disease and tuberculous meningitis. Protection against adult pulmonary tuberculosis varies widely by region and prior environmental mycobacterial exposure. BCG can cause local ulceration and lymphadenitis, while disseminated BCG disease signals severe immune deficiency such as SCID or profound T cell dysfunction and requires urgent specialist management.
steps.say: BCG chiefly protects young children from disseminated and meningeal tuberculosis, not every pulmonary case.

left.title: Benefits and effects
points: Strongest evidence against severe childhood forms
Variable pulmonary protection by geography
Normal local papule ulcer and scar sequence
Regional nodes may enlarge transiently

right.title: Safety warnings
points: Avoid in known severe immunodeficiency
Disseminated BCG suggests SCID or advanced immune failure
Suppurative lymphadenitis may need aspiration
BCG does not make IGRA positive

steps.tx: **MDR TB** means resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the two most powerful first line drugs. Pre XDR and XDR categories add fluoroquinolone and other priority drug resistance according to current definitions. Treatment uses longer all oral regimens built from susceptibility results and drug availability, often including bedaquiline, linezolid and a fluoroquinolone. Every additional resistance result can remove a drug and reshape the regimen.
steps.say: MDR means both isoniazid and rifampicin are lost; modern category labels follow additional priority drug resistance.

nodes.label: LPA and culture DST expand profile

steps.tx: The **niacin test** exploits accumulation of niacin in culture medium by Mycobacterium tuberculosis because it cannot efficiently convert niacin to NAD. A reagent strip or chemical test turns positive, historically helping distinguish M tuberculosis from Mycobacterium bovis, which is usually niacin negative. Molecular identification and MPT64 antigen testing now provide faster modern routes, but the biochemical logic remains a classic examination distinction.
steps.say: Niacin accumulation supports M tuberculosis and helps contrast it with usually niacin negative M bovis.

left.title: M tuberculosis clues
points: Niacin accumulation positive
Nitrate reduction usually positive
MPT64 antigen positive in many rapid tests
Rough buff colonies on LJ

right.title: M bovis clues
points: Usually niacin and nitrate negative
Dysgonic growth improved by pyruvate
Intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance
Associated historically with unpasteurised milk

steps.tx: **Sputum smear grading** uses standardised scales based on the number of acid fast bacilli per number of microscopic fields examined. Higher grades correlate with cavitation, transmission risk and delayed conversion during treatment. Follow up smears monitor response but can remain positive from dead organisms, which is why culture conversion carries stronger evidence of sterilising activity in drug resistant disease and clinical trials.
steps.say: Smear grade estimates burden and infectiousness, whereas culture conversion better tracks living bacilli.

left.title: Uses of grading
points: Prioritises infection control urgency
Supports household contact assessment
Predicts longer time to negativity
Standardises reporting between laboratories

right.title: Monitoring caveats
points: ZN stains viable and dead bacilli
Fluorescence grades require defined field counts
Culture may convert before smear clears
Worsening grade prompts adherence and resistance review

steps.tx: When molecular and phenotypic tests disagree, the isolate should not be forced into a single convenient label. **Repeat testing, sequencing and reference laboratory review** can reveal heteroresistance, mixed infection, disputed rpoB mutations or low level resistance missed by critical concentration methods. Treatment history and clinical response are part of the laboratory interpretation, not an afterthought, and specimens should be saved for arbitration.
steps.say: Discordant resistance results signal heteroresistance or disputed mutations and deserve reference laboratory arbitration.

left.title: Reasons for discordance
points: Mixed susceptible and resistant populations
Silent or disputed gene mutations
Low bacterial load and sampling variation
Phenotypic critical concentration borderline

right.title: Safe response
points: Repeat molecular test on fresh specimen
Send culture for sequencing and phenotypic DST
Avoid prematurely discarding an effective drug
Consult TB and reference laboratory specialists
